dedupe_keys.name: saint scenario analysis interface for energy systems for coupled gas pipeline and electricity networks

description: SAInt, the Scenario Analysis Interface for Energy Systems, is encoord's software for modelling energy markets and coupled energy networks. For gas, it runs steady-state and dynamic hydraulic simulations of transmission and distribution pipeline networks to track pressure and linepack; plans assets including pipelines, compressor stations, valves, regulators, underground storage, LNG regasification terminals, demands and supplies; tracks gas quality, composition and temperature for hydrogen injection and blending; schedules LNG arrivals and storage operation; and runs Monte Carlo simulations to quantify the impact of extreme events and plan mitigation. Its coupled module combines power flow with gas hydraulics to model interdependencies at gas-fired plants, power-to-gas units, electric compressors and storage, and to quantify correlated impacts of extreme events on both networks. Coverage: user-built networks, with model-ready datasets on its user forum. Format and access: desktop software with a free 30-day trial licence after forum approval. Licence and cost: commercial. Caveats: proprietary and documented mostly through vendor pages and guides. It supports cascading failure, resilience and capacity planning of gas pipeline networks and their coupling with power grids. It relates to the US National Pipeline Mapping System and CER pipeline profiles in the catalogue.
